auxiliary_material: The abstract notes early results revealed promising improvements in treatment outcomes with the high fiber diet intervention but focuses primarily on systemic immunity profiling rather than detailed human microbiome compositional analysis. The study highlights that circulating monocyte levels are known to negatively correlate with ICB response and warrants further mechanistic study on dietary fiber mediated regulation of peripheral immunity. Subgroup analysis indicated findings were more prominent in those receiving combination nivolumab + ipilimumab compared to monotherapy, though sample sizes were small (n=3 vs n=7).
outline_action: Cite this study as evidence that the DIET trial is reporting immune profiling outcomes and suggests microbiome dependence via FMT models. Use the immune profiling data (monocyte reduction, T cell activation) to support the biological plausibility of diet-ICI interaction. Flag that the specific human microbiome mediation analysis required by the gap question remains unidentified in this abstract and may require locating subsequent full-text publications or companion papers focusing on metagenomics.
remaining_gap: This material does not fulfill the success criteria for specific gut microbiome compositional or functional changes in humans associated with the dietary intervention, nor does it report a statistical mediation analysis linking microbiome changes to ICI clinical outcomes (ORR, PFS, OS). While FMT results suggest microbiome dependence, the specific taxa or pathways mediating the effect in humans are not identified in this text, and there is no explicit statement that microbiome mediation data is pending or unavailable, only that further mechanistic study is warranted.
useful_material: This study reports secondary objectives of the DIET trial (NCT04645680), a phase II randomized double-blinded dietary intervention in melanoma patients receiving immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Patients were randomized (2:1) to a high fiber diet (30-50 g/d) or healthy control diet (20 g/d). The authors measured peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) using NanoString gene expression and CyTOF mass cytometry. Findings included decreased abundance scores of circulating macrophages, neutrophils, classical monocytes, and dendritic cells, alongside higher T cell activation gene signatures in the high fiber arm versus control within week 5-8. Human-to-mouse fecal microbiota transplant (FMT) studies using patient stool collected pre or post intervention revealed improved ICB response in mice receiving post-high fiber diet stool, suggesting microbiome-dependent benefits.
